# Day of China

> Day of China teaches Chinese traditional culture the way it is actually lived — one ordinary day at a time. An English-language guide for curious beginners: eleven moments from 6:30 a.m. Ba Duan Jin and Tai Chi in the park to a 9 p.m. foot soak, timed to the old twelve two-hour periods.

## Moments

- [Ba Duan Jin and Tai Chi in the park](https://dayofchina.com/moments/ba-duan-jin-tai-chi/): 6:30 a.m., 卯时. Morning exercise: the Eight Brocades and Tai Chi.
- [The wet market](https://dayofchina.com/moments/wet-market/): 10:30 a.m., 巳时. Buying the day's food fresh, by hand.
- [Start the soup](https://dayofchina.com/moments/simmering-soup/): 4 p.m., 申时. Slow-simmered soup by the solar terms.
- [All moments](https://dayofchina.com/moments/): The full day, eleven moments.

## Guides

- [Tai Chi guide](https://dayofchina.com/guides/tai-chi/): The first guide — the full morning routine as a printable PDF. Coming soon, $9.99 on Etsy.
- [All guides](https://dayofchina.com/guides/): Printable PDF guides, one per moment.

- [What is Day of China?](https://dayofchina.com/about/): The twelve two-hour periods and how the site works.
